questions.question: What should SingEDoc help people accomplish?
questions.answer: A web e-signature app where a sender uploads a document, invites recipients to sign it, tracks signing status, and downloads the completed document. Treat nonprofitanchor-website-privacy-notice.docx as a proposed sample document; it is not present in the workspace.
questions.rationale: Inferred from the user's request to share files with people who need to sign them. A DOCX filename was provided, but no matching file is available in the workspace.
questions.recommendedChoice: A web e-signature app where a sender uploads a document, invites recipients to sign it, tracks signing status, and downloads the completed document.

questions.question: Who will use the app, and what should each type of user be able to do?
questions.answer: Senders sign in to upload documents, invite recipients, and track progress. Recipients open a secure signing link and sign without creating an account.
questions.rationale: A sender account plus recipient signing links is a low-friction MVP default; recipient identity and access policy can be refined during review.
questions.recommendedChoice: Senders sign in to upload documents, invite recipients, and track progress. Recipients open a secure signing link and sign without creating an account.

questions.question: Where should people use the app?
questions.rationale: A browser-based app is a practical starting point, but the platform should match your intended users.

options.label: Web app
options.description: Use in a browser on desktop and mobile.

options.label: Mobile app
options.description: A native or cross-platform phone/tablet app.

questions.question: Which language should the app interface use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript is a strong default for a new app interface.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing to JavaScript; recommended for maintainable apps.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use standard JavaScript without TypeScript annotations.

questions.question: Do you have a preferred frontend framework or UI library?
questions.rationale: No frontend stack preference has been provided; you can choose a framework or enter another preference.

questions.question: Which language should the signing and document API use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript supports a consistent, maintainable stack for the React client and API.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Shared language and types across the React app and API.

questions.question: Do you prefer Azure Functions or a custom backend framework? If custom, enter the framework name.
questions.rationale: Azure Functions is a practical MVP default for document and signing API operations; a custom framework can be specified instead.

questions.question: What information or files should the app save or manage? Select any relevant storage, or choose no datastore if nothing needs to persist.
questions.rationale: The app needs relational records for users, invitations, and signing status, plus private file storage for originals and completed documents.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The app does not need to save data or files.

options.label: Azure Blob Storage
options.description: Uploaded documents, images, or other files.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to use the app's features?
questions.rationale: Senders need authenticated access to manage documents and signing requests. Recipient access can use scoped signing links in the MVP and does not imply recipient accounts.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users have accounts and sign in to access app features.

options.label: No
options.description: The app's features do not require users to sign in.
